read_only_audit.kind: Independent source review; not an additional test execution
story_scope: KAN-29 historical preservation and superseding submission policy
read_only_audit.scope_note: Reviewed relevant source sections and timing/isolation patterns; do not interpret the list as a fresh assertion-by-assertion verification of every related suite. Other owned stories were reviewed separately by root/another reviewer.

findings.finding: Unfiltered status locator matches both the conflict notice and loading message during queue refresh.
findings.repair: Hold refresh response to force overlap, scope notice locator by its text, release in finally and await completed empty queue.

findings.finding: Conflict notice and absence of old rows establish refresh started, not completed.
findings.repair: Await final empty-state heading and assert exactly two queue reads.

findings.finding: Released held writes were followed immediately by absence assertions that could pass before async completion.
findings.repair: Register cancellation listener before logout; release held response in finally; await fixture write completion and request failure before final signed-out and absence checks.

positive_observations: KAN-65 success-status assertion is already filtered by message.
Component lifecycle tests settle deferred responses and reset state; cleanup removes components and stubbed globals.
Backend transaction tests use local mocks and awaited calls.
Integration fixtures use random isolated schemas and matching application_name; locking scenarios poll actual PostgreSQL lock waits, clean up in finally and await pending operations.
Timestamp bounds use database clocks and auth tokens use relative expiry.
KAN-29 regression scope retains automatic-assignment history while testing the KAN-79 replacement submission policy.
No equivalent ambiguous status locator was identified in supplemental KAN-52 review.
read_only_audit.patch_review: No blocking issue in the three-file patch. The completion barriers have no successful-path dependency cycle; finally does not catch or suppress route errors. Browser logout tests establish cancellation and final UI state, while component tests exercise callbacks settling after account/navigation changes.

evidence_boundaries: The before-fix run uses a deliberately held queue refresh and the original broad status assertion; it is a deterministic reproduction, not an unchanged-main rerun.
Browser fixtures substitute authenticated API responses: they prove UI behavior/session lifecycle, not live end-to-end database or Supabase acceptance.
Browser reporter JSON does not expose repeatEachIndex. Attempts are retained by unique reporter instance ID and ordered by actual start time; retry is reported exactly.
No per-case passes are inferred from aggregate-only logs. Selected unit/component per-case outcomes are separately retained in AUTO-20261021-KAN79-07 JSON.
No hosted/manual test execution, story acceptance, Jira status, sprint velocity or Definition of Done completion is established.
Repeated local passes reduce observed flakiness risk but do not guarantee no future flakes.
Raw browser config and webServer environment are intentionally omitted to exclude connection credentials.

atomic_browser_cases.scenario: Conflict feedback remains correct while the Lead queue refresh is pending
atomic_browser_cases.steps: 1. Open the fixture Lead queue and select its available coordinator. 2. Return COORDINATOR_ALREADY_ASSIGNED to the single assignment PUT and hold the resulting queue GET. 3. While held, check the conflict notice, loading status, disabled Refresh and absence of Open allocation. 4. Release the GET with an empty queue and wait for the final empty-state heading. 5. Check the retained conflict notice, absent loading/success link and request counts.
atomic_browser_cases.data: Event 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000079; coordinator 10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000029; assignment HTTP 409; initial queue has one request and refreshed queue is empty.
atomic_browser_cases.expected: Conflict and loading notices coexist without a locator ambiguity. After refresh the empty queue is visible, the conflict remains, loading disappears and no success link is shown. Exactly one assignment PUT and two queue GETs occur, with no unexpected API request.

specification.scenario_outline: KAN-8: Reconcile a conflicting or uncertain booking decision without repeating the write
specification.preconditions: Use isolated component fetch mocks or intercepted browser API fixtures with an authorised Venue Staff user and one pending booking. Never send fixture writes or failure injection to shared Supabase.
specification.test_steps: 1. Submit one approval. 2. In the conflict variant return BOOKING_ALREADY_DECIDED and supply the competing rejected outcome on the automatic read. 3. In the uncertain variant fail the write response, then select Refresh booking to retrieve the saved outcome. 4. Inspect the displayed outcome, decision controls and recorded POST count.
specification.test_data: Pending booking booking-a in components or 80000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 in browser fixtures; APPROVED attempt; conflict HTTP 409 with competing REJECTED decision; uncertain network failure in components or HTTP 500 after fixture save in browser.
specification.expected_result: The conflict retains its error message and displays the competing decision information without a second write. An uncertain response hides decision controls and requires explicit refresh before displaying the saved outcome information and reason. Each variant records exactly one decision POST.
specification.specification_notes: Documents existing recovery safeguards around an approval attempt and the correct booking outcome; no new customer criterion. The competing rejection is fixture data, not an executed rejection action, so AC4 is not claimed. Browser APIs are response fixtures, not live persistence or hosted acceptance.

specification.scenario_outline: KAN-8: Enforce the implemented booking decision reason length boundary
specification.preconditions: Use the booking decision parser unit suite and an isolated Venue Staff detail component with a mocked pending booking.
specification.test_steps: 1. Parse a REJECTED decision with a reason of exactly 2,000 characters. 2. Parse the same decision with 2,001 characters. 3. In the detail component select Reject booking and set a 2,001-character reason through the test input event. 4. Inspect the validation feedback, submit button and fetch count.
specification.test_data: Parser reasons: 'a' repeated 2000 and 2001 times; component reason: 'x' repeated 2001 times; decision REJECTED; initial pending booking fetch only.
specification.expected_result: The parser accepts exactly 2,000 characters and rejects 2,001. The component displays the 2,000-character limit, disables Record decision and makes no decision request for the over-limit value.
specification.specification_notes: The 2,000-character limit is an existing implementation boundary, not a newly agreed customer requirement. Exact-limit acceptance is asserted at parser level; this case does not claim an exact-limit browser submission or database write.

specification.scenario_outline: KAN-16: Retry a temporary request read failure without displaying stale data
specification.preconditions: Render the organiser request list or detail with an authorised synthetic organiser and isolated fetch mocks. No hosted account or database is used.
specification.test_steps: 1. Fail the initial list read with a network error and, in a separate variant, a service-unavailable response. 2. Fail the initial detail read with a service-unavailable response. 3. Verify each failure view has no request data, select Try again and return the successful fixture. 4. Inspect the request display, cleared error and read count.
specification.test_data: List variants: TypeError('Network failure') and HTTP 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE; detail variant: HTTP 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE; successful fixture request a named Career fair; one initial GET and one retry GET per variant.
specification.expected_result: Each failed read displays an error without stale request data. Try again performs one additional read, displays the successful request fixture and clears the error.
specification.specification_notes: Documents existing UI read-failure/retry behavior supporting the accessible request display in AC1. The tests do not perform a successful submission/review followed by reload, so they do not claim AC2 coverage. Component fixtures establish rendering and request sequencing, not live service recovery.

specification.scenario_outline: KAN-16: Discard delayed request data after an organiser account change or sign-out
specification.preconditions: Use isolated reactive-session component fixtures with organiser-1 and organiser-2. Hold the old request read using a deferred response; use synthetic request data only.
specification.test_steps: 1. Start a list or detail read for organiser-1 and hold its response. 2. Switch to organiser-2 and finish the replacement read; then release the old response. 3. In a separate detail variant load private data, start and hold Refresh, sign out, then release that response. 4. Inspect the current account view, previous request fields and aborted signals.
specification.test_data: List account switch: old request a named Previous account event and new request b named New account event. Detail account switch: old Career fair with Suitable event. reason and replacement HTTP 404. Sign-out variant: initially decided request, then a held refresh returning the old detail.
specification.expected_result: Changing identity aborts the old read. Its late response cannot replace the new account's list, disclose the previous detail or restore private data after sign-out. The signed-out detail shows a sign-in-required message and the denied replacement detail remains unavailable.
specification.specification_notes: Documents client-side stale-response/privacy safeguards supporting AC1 and AC3. These component tests assert absence of protected content after identity changes; they do not prove the direct API authorisation required by AC3. Server authorisation, hosted session expiry and token reuse need their separate integration/manual cases.

specification.scenario_outline: KAN-36: Reconcile an uncertain decision or failed post-save refresh using reads only
specification.preconditions: Render the review detail with isolated fetch mocks for eligible request a and an authorised coordinator context; stub unrelated planning panels. Each scenario starts from a fresh fixture.
specification.test_steps: 1. Choose approval once. 2. In one variant return a confirmed successful write followed by a failed detail read; select Try again. 3. In separate variants return a network write error or REVIEW_ALREADY_DECIDED; select Refresh request. 4. Supply the saved approved detail and inspect feedback, controls and POST count.
specification.test_data: Request a named Career fair, coordinator-1, decision APPROVED; confirmed write HTTP 201 then TypeError('Network failure'); uncertain write TypeError('Network failure'); competing-write HTTP 409 REVIEW_ALREADY_DECIDED; final approved detail with one recorded review.
specification.expected_result: A confirmed save with failed refresh is described as saved but awaiting current details. An uncertain or conflicting write requires refresh before another choice. Each recovery displays the saved approved outcome and uses a GET rather than repeating the single decision POST.
specification.specification_notes: Documents existing uncertainty and reconciliation safeguards; it does not change approval policy. It complements TC-04-230's persisted repeat-decision checks and does not claim database persistence from mocks.

specification.scenario_outline: KAN-36: Ignore late review responses after changing request or leaving the page
specification.preconditions: Use isolated review component fixtures for requests a and b, with a deferred old read or write response and a memory router. No shared account or database is used.
specification.test_steps: 1. Submit approval for request a and hold the response. 2. Navigate to request b and render its detail, then release the old write as either success or conflict. 3. Repeat with an old detail read resolved after navigation. 4. In a separate write variant unmount the page before releasing success. 5. Inspect the current request, feedback and additional reads.
specification.test_data: Old request a named Career fair; current request b named Community lunch; late write HTTP 201 recorded approval or HTTP 409 REVIEW_ALREADY_DECIDED; delayed old detail response; unmounted success response.
specification.expected_result: Late responses cannot replace request b or add request a's approval/conflict feedback to it. Request b retains its own enabled decision control. Completing a write after unmount does not trigger another detail read.
specification.specification_notes: Documents client-side route-version and unmount guards supporting correct-request approval feedback under AC1. No transaction or competing committed outcome is asserted here, so AC4 is not claimed. This case covers navigation/unmount, not a delayed review response across a session switch.
